lines: לַאדֹנָי כָּבוֹד, כִּי הוּא נָתַן לָנוּ

review: The hymn is the victory procession of Psalm 68:18 and Colossians 2:15: 1:1–4 is John 19:30 (נִשְׁלַם) with Rev 5:9, 3:1–2 Ps 68:19 (עָלִיתָ לַמָּרוֹם שָׁבִיתָ שֶּׁבִי) with Isa 49:25, and 4:1–2 Rev 5:12 and 7:10.

1:1–3 repeats the same line three times, exactly as the printed تَمَّ الْخَلَاصُ هَلِّلُويَا رَنِّمُوا is set three times before the short address; the Hebrew does not vary the three lines, because the repetition is the stanza's whole form and the third line leads straight into the acclamation of line 4.
1:4 לַאֲדֹנֵינוּ יֵשׁוּעַ — the printed short line is لِرَبِّنَا يَسُوع, four words against the long triple; the Hebrew keeps the brevity, so the stanza ends on a name and not on a clause.

2:3 נִצָּחוֹן עוֹלָם — the Arabic بِنَصْرٍ دَائِمٍ is 'with a lasting victory'; the Hebrew uses נִצָּחוֹן, the noun of 1 Sam 15:29 and 1 Chr 29:11 for the eternal triumph that belongs to God, so the army's win is His and not its own.

3:1 רָמַס כֹּחוֹת שְׁאוֹל — the Arabic دَاسَ قُوَّاتِ الْجَحِيمِ is 'trampled the powers of hell'; רָמַס is the biblical verb for treading down (Isa 63:3, פּוּרָה דָּרַכְתִּי לְבַדִּי), and שְׁאוֹל is kept instead of a later hell-word, because the line is about the powers and not the place.
